title: Tamper Evidence: The Seal's Job
description: A tamper-evident seal does not prevent intrusion — it makes intrusion visible: the seal breaks, marks, or changes in ways that cannot be undone invisibly. Numbered seals tie the physical evidence to a log. The seal's job is to answer 'was this opened?' with certainty.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Numbered Security Seals
description: Numbered seals carry unique serials — laser-etched or printed — logged at application and verified at inspection. Duplicate numbers reveal substitution. The number is the identity; the log is the memory. Sequential issuance prevents gaps.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: Cable Seals: Locking Hasps and Doors
title: Cable Seals: Locking Hasps and Doors
description: Cable seals thread steel cable through hasps and lock with a one-way mechanism — cut to remove, numbered body for logging. ISO 17712 grades them (indicative, security, high-security) by pull and tamper tests. Shipping containers and equipment racks use them by the thousand.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Tamper-Evident Tape
description: Tamper-evident tape bonds to cartons and chassis and fractures or leaves VOID patterns when peeled — the adhesive is engineered to fail visibly. Heat or solvents that defeat cheap tape fail against proper constructions. Tape is the seal for things that ship.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Security Labels and Stickers
description: Security labels combine numbering, barcodes, holograms, and destructible substrates into one inspection point for equipment and documents. A label that transfers cleanly is a failed label. Layered features raise the forgery bar.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: ISO 17712: The Seal Standard
description: ISO 17712 classifies mechanical seals — indicative (I), security (S), high-security (H) — with pull-strength, shear, and tamper tests per grade. Customs and C-TPAT programs recognize H seals on containers. The grade must match the risk.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: Seal Logs and Chain of Custody
title: Seal Logs and Chain of Custody
description: Every seal application and removal gets logged — number, location, time, person — building the chain of custody that makes the seal meaningful. An unlogged seal is decoration. Audits reconcile logs against physical inventory.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Inspection: Reading the Evidence
description: Inspection compares seal numbers to the log, checks bodies for tool marks, and verifies tape patterns — trained eyes, good light, and a checklist. Inspections happen on receipt, on schedule, and on suspicion. The procedure is the product.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Defeating Seals: What Attackers Try
description: Attackers try to lift tape with heat, pick cable seals, or substitute numbered bodies — which is why seals use destructible materials, one-way locks, and controlled issuance. Knowing the attacks shapes the selection. Defense assumes a skilled adversary.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Seals on Equipment Racks
description: Server and comms racks get numbered seals on doors and panels so unauthorized access leaves evidence — datacenter techs log every break. Combined with access logs, seals complete the physical audit trail. The rack tells on intruders.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Seals in Transit
description: High-value shipments travel under seal — container doors, crates, and cases numbered and logged at each handoff. Receiving inspects before signing. The handoff log is where custody transfers and liability follows.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Electronic Seals (E-Seals)
description: E-seals add electronics — RFID reporting seal state, some with tamper sensors and GPS — marrying physical evidence with digital logs. A cut cable reports itself. The seal becomes a sensor.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Forensic Value of Seals
description: Intact seals are evidence of integrity; broken seals are evidence of intrusion — both admissible when the chain of custody is documented. Courts understand numbered logs. The seal program's paperwork is its legal power.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Seal Program Management
description: A seal program manages procurement (controlled vendors), issuance (sequential, signed out), inspection (trained, scheduled), and disposal (destroyed, logged). The program is the security; the seal is just the token. Maturity shows in the logs.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The Complete Tamper-Evidence Picture
description: Ladder-top seals: numbered identity, destructible materials, graded standards, logged custody, trained inspection. Fifteen rungs from a sticker to a physical audit trail that stands up in court.
